name: beaver-sim
$comment: The flyable DHC-2 Beaver: the FDC airframe with the engine/propeller drivetrain (switchable), the cockpit controls and the FDC autopilot (pitch/altitude hold, roll/heading hold, turn coordinator), with the FMU interface as export markers. The default run is the demo: a climb, a turn to 090 and a level-off. Generated by design/build_model.py; see the README.

annotations.text: **Airframe.** RigidBody3D on its principal axes (the product of inertia Jxz tilts them 1.16 deg from the body x axis); the air and engine wrench (BeaverWrench) is a modulated source on the body, applied in the geometric body frame through the Mount.

**Drivetrain (bond graph, our addition).** 1-junction Crank: engine torque P(pz, n, rho)/w (MSe), crank + propeller inertia I = 12 kg m^2, the propeller's torque -Q (MSe) from the governor of the constant-speed propeller, tachometer (SpeedSensor, which makes the bond graph rotational). Global `drivetrain`: 1 the thrust comes from the shaft power Q w, 0 from the source's algebraic power at the commanded rpm (exact FDC).
**Inputs.** The ExportInputPass markers pass the demo and test stimulus (the globals) through in bg-sim; in the FMU the host drives them.

**Autopilot (FDC 'Beaver', REP ch. 11).** Pitch: attitude hold (PAH) and altitude hold (ALH); roll: attitude hold (RAH), heading hold (HH) and the turn coordinator; gains scheduled on V. Servos (our fit of FDC's actuator models): 0.09 s lag with the speed-dependent cable gain.

options.text: 45 m/s at 6000 ft on the FDC autopilot. The demo: **climb** power and +4 deg at 5 s, **turn** to the heading at 30 s (heading hold), **level off** at the altitude (altitude hold) at 70 s, cruise power at 85 s. Move the sliders, or switch the autopilot off (mode 0) and fly the test inputs.
